correctness.rationale: For n-bit N with digit sum/Hamming weight w>=2, first recurrence continuation is K_{n+1}=w; subtract consecutive window sums to get K_{n+j}=2^(j-1)w-P_{j-1} for 1<=j<=n+1. Strict increasing after w and K_{2n+1}=2^n w-N>N restrict a hit to j<=n. The bounds 2^(j-1)(w-1)<N<=2^(j-1)w and 2^(n-1)<=N<2^n force j=n-ceil(log_2 w)+1 (examine boundary w=2^c). Write L=2^c,N=PL+S, 0<=S<L; the hit equation becomes 2^(n-c)w=(L+1)P+S, uniquely determining P,S by Euclidean division. The bitcount equation is necessary and sufficient, as the converse constructs n bits and verifies the hit. Weight one numbers are powers of two. Hence at most n per bit length and B2(x)<=h(h+1)/2. Independent direct complete recurrence enumeration for n=2..16 matched this construction exactly; infinite conclusion relies on algebra, not the test.
